solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One who takes exercise or goes after a bit of cash

indicators.note: goes after places the exercise-and-or pair behind the bit of cash
a bit of the word cash means just its opening part is used here

parts.note: the opening pair of letters of cash is used
PT stands for physical training, i.e. exercise
or is used as written

explanation.surface: A description of someone who either works out or chases a little money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who takes' reads like a sportsperson, but it defines someone who seizes a prisoner; 'goes after' sets the exercise and 'or' behind the bit of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A captor is a person who seizes and holds a prisoner.

parts.note: the camel is called the ship of the desert

indicators.note: back means the word for pain is read from its end

parts.note: an ail is a pain or ailment

explanation.surface: A camel suffering from back pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle is topical: the Masters at Augusta National, where every hole is named after a plant, so '10' means the tenth hole. 'back' turns the word for pain round.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth hole at Augusta National golf club is named after this flowering shrub.

indicators.note: roasted suggests cooking the letters into a new arrangement

parts.note: 9-down's solution, the jelly
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A recipe line: a roasted nut, served hot.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' points to 9-down, ASPIC; with I and HOT, 'roasted' rearranges the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The green-kernelled pistachio is a popular snack nut.

clue.text: What vigorous 26 may do on next page

explanation.walkthrough: 26 is TREE, so the first sense reads OVER-LEAF: to produce leaves in excess.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigorous tree may sprout too much foliage; and a note marked so is continued on the reverse side of the sheet.

indicators.note: abused means mistreated, so the letters are knocked into a new order
headless means the word flamingo loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone mistreats a flamingo with no head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' leaves LAMINGO, which 'abused' rearranges; A follows. '5' is Augusta's fifth hole.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth hole at Augusta National is named after this flowering tree.

clue.text: Giving change to Guardian with posh replacement

indicators.note: change tells us the resulting letters are reordered
replacement says one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: U means upper-class or posh

explanation.surface: A newspaper notice about giving a change to the Guardian with a posh replacement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' swaps U (posh) in GUARDIAN for W (with), giving GWARDIAN; 'change' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Awarding a prize means bestowing or handing it over.

indicators.note: injury means the letters are damaged into a new order
last picks the final letter of the word minute

explanation.surface: A footballer dreads a last-minute hamstring injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' takes E from 'minute'; 'injury' rearranges E plus HAMSTRING.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightmares are bad dreams, things one dreads or fears.

clue.text: Starts lifting a slightly enlarged roof beam

indicators.note: starts asks for the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Builders begin raising a slightly bigger roof beam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts' takes the first letters of 'lifting a slightly enlarged roof'.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser produces an intense narrow beam of light.

parts.note: Z is the final letter of the alphabet
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Ordering a last beer, at hole thirteen.
explanation.walkthrough: '13' is the thirteenth hole at Augusta.
explanation.definitionFit: The thirteenth hole at Augusta National bears the name of this flowering shrub.

clue.text: Jelly and ice-cream starters on when quiet

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

indicators.note: starters asks for the opening letters of the hyphenated ice-cream

explanation.surface: A dessert of jelly and ice cream starters served when all is quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' takes I and C from 'ice-cream'; 'on' sets them beneath AS and P.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made with meat stock.

explanation.surface: Could checkers be today's competition?
explanation.definitionFit: Chess or draughts experts are masters; and the Masters is the golf tournament played at Augusta, topical on the day.

indicators.note: first puts the word for majestic before the A

parts.note: august means majestic or venerable

explanation.surface: A grand starter at a dinner: a majestic first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' places AUGUST before A.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta National in Georgia is the golf course that hosts the Masters.

clue.text: Frenchman has assignation in second home

indicators.note: has means the Frenchman's name holds another word inside

parts.note: Pierre is a typical French man's name
a date is an assignation or rendezvous

explanation.surface: A Frenchman keeps a lover's tryst at his second home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is the container signal: the Frenchman's name holds the assignation, and 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied-a-terre is a small secondary residence, often in a city.

clue.text: Shaw's Eliza, for example, river maid

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, crossword slang for a river
a maid is a girl

explanation.surface: Eliza Doolittle from Shaw's Pygmalion described as a maid by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In cryptics 'river' often hides FLOWER, read as flow-er, a thing that flows. Eliza Doolittle in Pygmalion sells flowers in Covent Garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza Doolittle in Pygmalion is a Cockney who sells flowers on the street.

indicators.note: following places the word for healthy after in

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: Something healthy follows from dressing in drag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' is a verb here: to draw on a cigarette, not cross-dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag on a cigarette is to breathe its smoke in.

indicators.note: roam means wander, so the letters of men stray into a new order
rough seas are churned up, so its letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Sailors wander over rough seas as a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roam' turns MEN into ENM, 'rough' turns SEAS into ASSE.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is French-derived for all at once, as a body.

clue.text: Recoverd from drinking beer mixed with head of distillery's starter round

indicators.note: round means the starter's word goes around the other letters

parts.note: soup is a classic first course or starter

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of beer are reshuffled
head of takes the first letter of distillery's

explanation.surface: A man who recovered from a binge by mixing beer with a distillery chief's offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' looks like a container signal but belongs to the definition; 'mixed' shuffles the beer, and 'round' wraps the starter around it. 'Recoverd' is printed so.
explanation.definitionFit: Sobered up means became clear-headed again after intoxication.

indicators.note: renovated means rebuilt, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Thinking about the cottage I renovated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovated' rearranges COTTAGE plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: To cogitate is to think deeply or ponder.

clue.text: Senile dogs go out wandering with inertia

indicators.note: wandering means the letters stray into another order
out means the letters of go are removed from dogs

explanation.surface: Old dogs wander off, showing sluggishness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go out' strips GO from DOGS leaving DS; 'wandering' rearranges SENILE plus DS.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is laziness, a lack of activity like inertia.

indicators.note: after places the shoot word behind the blood word

parts.note: red is the colour of blood
a bud is a young shoot on a plant

explanation.surface: A gardener's shoot ends up after blood, perhaps of a Communist pal.
explanation.walkthrough: '16' is Augusta's sixteenth hole. The bracket gives a second route: RED (Communist) + BUD (friend).
explanation.definitionFit: The sixteenth hole at Augusta National is named after this small flowering tree.

indicators.note: internal says one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a tinge is a slight shade of colour

explanation.surface: A shade of colour accompanied by internal pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internal' puts W (with) inside TINGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinge is a sudden sharp pang.

clue.text: We've struck trail with club at 11

indicators.note: 've, short for have, means we holds another word within it

parts.note: struck means hit
to dog someone is to trail them
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Golfers who struck a trail with a club at the eleventh.
explanation.walkthrough: ''ve' (have) is the container signal, making 'We' hold the word for struck. '11' is the eleventh hole at Augusta.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh hole at Augusta National is named after this flowering tree.

clue.text: Spooner instructed a spirit to be unbreakable

indicators.note: Spooner signals that the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: taught means instructed
a wight is a spirit or ghostly creature

explanation.surface: Dr Spooner taught a ghost how to be indestructible.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of TAUGHT A WIGHT gives 'waught a tight', said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Watertight means firm and impossible to fault, like an unbreakable alibi.

clue.text: Drink preserved by pouring it on ice

indicators.note: preserved by means the answer is kept within the following words

explanation.surface: A drink kept fresh by pouring it over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preserved by' shows the answer is held in 'it on ice'; 'pouring' is surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is a mixer drink, often poured over ice.

parts.note: an environmental campaigner is jokingly called a hugger of this plant, and every hole in the puzzle is named for one

explanation.definitionFit: Green activists are nicknamed huggers of woody plants, and plants are the puzzle's theme.

explanation.surface: Is the cat perhaps back from Argentina?
explanation.definitionFit: A puma is a big wild cat; and Argentina's rugby team are the Pumas, so a back in that side is one.

clue.text: Darling dog keeps row 17 (in Barbican and in Apollo)

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the bracketed venue names

explanation.surface: A darling dog making a racket at seventeen, in two London venues.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket hides the answer in 'Barbican and in Apollo'. The rest is a second route: NANA, the Darling family's dog in Peter Pan, keeps DIN (row). '17' is Augusta's seventeenth hole.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventeenth hole at Augusta National is named after this shrub, heavenly bamboo.

clue.text: Lettuce head turned out badly in roll

indicators.note: out badly means the letters go wrong and are rearranged
head takes the first letter of lettuce

explanation.surface: A lettuce turned out badly in a sandwich roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes L from 'Lettuce'; 'out badly' rearranges L plus TURNED.
explanation.definitionFit: To trundle is to roll along slowly and heavily.

indicators.note: on places the light after the exhibition hall

parts.note: ExCeL is a large exhibition centre in East London
an LED is a light-emitting diode

explanation.surface: Someone shone a light on an exhibition hall.
explanation.walkthrough: ExCeL is a London exhibition and conference centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to stand out, the way someone shone at a task.

indicators.note: on radio means the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: pampers means spoils or indulges

explanation.surface: A broadcast about spoils, on Radio 7.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech, 'pampers' sounds the same as the answer. '7' is Augusta's seventh hole.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventh hole at Augusta National is named after the ornamental grass of this name.
